answer_text:
Here is a comprehensive guide to paying your **federal taxes online**:

---

## 💻 How to Pay Federal Taxes Online (IRS)

The IRS offers several convenient online payment options. You can visit the official IRS payments page at **[IRS.gov/payments](https://www.irs.gov/payments)**.

---

### ✅ Payment Options

#### 1. 🏦 IRS Direct Pay (Free – No Fees)
Pay personal or business taxes directly from your bank account with IRS Direct Pay. It's free and secure.
- Use Direct Pay online to make an individual tax payment from your checking or savings account without registration.
- A single payment can't exceed $10 million. To make a higher payment, use the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS) or same-day wire.

#### 2. 🏛️ IRS Online Account (Free – No Fees)
Sign in or create an account to pay now or schedule a payment. You can pay your tax balance due, estimated payments, or part of a payment plan.
- Pay now or schedule payments up to a year in advance.

#### 3. 💳 Debit/Credit Card or Digital Wallet (Fees Apply)
You can pay online or over the phone. You can also pay using digital wallets such as PayPal and Click to Pay.
- Your card statement will list your payment as "United States Treasury Tax Payment" and your fee as "Tax Payment Convenience Fee" or something similar.

#### 4. 🔁 EFTPS – Electronic Federal Tax Payment System
Set up the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS) for individual or business tax payments.
- Register for EFTPS to make one-time or recurring payments from your checking or savings account.
- Note: New EFTPS accounts can take up to five business days to process.

#### 5. 📱 IRS2Go Mobile App
Use the IRS2Go app for easy and secure mobile payments.

---

### 📋 What Can You Pay Online?
You can pay your balance due, set up a payment plan, pay estimated taxes, and more. You can also view your amount due, payment plan details, payment history, and scheduled payments.

---

### 📅 Important Deadlines
- The filing deadline for 2025 tax returns is April 15, 2026.
- Payment for taxes you owe is due by the filing deadline even if you get a filing extension.
- Estimated taxes are paid quarterly based on the income you expect your business to receive in a year.

---

### ⚠️ Can't Pay in Full?
If you can't pay what you owe, you have options. There are several payment plan types: simple, streamlined, in-business trust fund express, guaranteed, and partial payment installment agreements. You can also check if you can settle your debt for less than you owe with an offer in compromise.

---

### 📌 Tips
- The IRS encourages you to pay your taxes in full because penalties and interest will continue to grow until you pay the full balance.
- The IRS has issued guidance that taxpayers may continue to make payments via check using existing forms and procedures until further notice, but while electronic payments remain the preferred and more secure method, transitioning now is recommended.

---

**🔗 Official IRS Payment Portal:** [https://www.irs.gov/payments](https://www.irs.gov/payments)
